title: Needlepatch session econ benchmark
summary: Lightweight benchmark exploring sessionized workload tradeoffs across prefetching, compact-batching, and kv-cache hit patterns. Emphasis on p90/p99 tail behavior versus $/1k queries at small sustained QPS (10-100).
content:
Purpose:
This note records a focused, reproducible micro-benchmark we ran to investigate how small-session workloads (median turn length 12 tokens) behave under three operational knobs: compact batch slots (smallbatch), opportunistic prefetch, and KV-cache priming. We call the combined measurement group the 'needlepatch' experiment set because it probes narrow slices of session shape and cache warmup patterns that typical burst analyses miss.

Scope and motivation:
- Target workload: conversational assistant with many short-lived sessions and occasional extended turns.
- QPS envelope: 10, 25, 50, 100 sustained (to emulate low-to-moderate production tenants).
- Business metric: cost per 1k requests (hosted costing model: $/1k token-equivalent) and p50/p90/p99 latency (ms) for end-to-end generation.
- Why unique: many existing reports focus on sustained concurrency or large bursts. This focuses on session churn + KV-cache dynamics where per-session warmups can dominate cost and tail latency.

Experiment setup (short):
- Model: open-variant-13B (FP16, two quant profiles Q3 and Q4 tested).
- Hardware: A100s (single-GPU serving slices), uniform network 10Gbps.
- Client pattern: Poisson session arrivals, average session length 4 turns, avg tokens/turn = 12, prompt prefix 40 tokens.
- Measurement window: 60m per run, discard first 5m for warmup where applicable.
- Trials: 5 runs per config, report median of medians.

Configs tested (labels):
- baseline: no kv-cache, smallbatch disabled, no prefetch
- kv-on: kv-cache enabled, naive priming disabled
- kv-primed: kv-cache enabled, session-aware priming on first request
- smallbatch: compact batching enabled (slot-duration 150ms)
- prefetch: opportunistic prefetch of likely next token prefixes (heuristic lambda=0.25)
- hybrid: kv-primed + smallbatch + prefetch

Representative numeric results (QPS=25, Q3 quant profile):

+----------------------+--------+--------+--------+-----------+
| config               | p50(ms)| p90(ms)| p99(ms)| $/1k req  |
+----------------------+--------+--------+--------+-----------+
| baseline             | 120    | 420    | 980    | 12.6      |
| kv-on                | 110    | 360    | 820    | 11.9      |
| kv-primed            | 95     | 260    | 480    | 10.4      |
| smallbatch           | 130    | 340    | 700    | 9.8       |
| prefetch             | 115    | 300    | 640    | 10.1      |
| hybrid               | 90     | 230    | 420    | 8.7       |
+----------------------+--------+--------+--------+-----------+

Notes on table: $/1k req is an amortized grouping including GPU fraction, energy overhead, and inferred slot idle costs. Numbers are intentionally coarse-grained to highlight relative deltas.

QPS sweep highlights (selected):
- At QPS=10: smallbatch shows larger relative cost savings (slot packing higher) but p99 variance increases because of slot tail jitter. Hybrid still leads in dollar efficiency but p99 is only modestly worse than kv-primed.
- At QPS=100: kv-primed benefits diminish (cache hit rates saturate) and smallbatch contention increases; prefetch overhead slightly raises cost but reduces p50.

KV-cache hit-rate crosstab (approx):
- baseline: 0%
- kv-on: 35%
- kv-primed: 62%
- hybrid: 68%

Mini ASCII sparkline (p99 trend across QPS for hybrid):
QPS: 10   25    50    100
p99: 520 - 420 - 390 - 440
spark: ▁▂▃▂

Observations and qualitative interpretation:
1) Priming investment pays off: actively priming the KV cache on the first turn reduces downstream decoding cost by cutting repeated attention computation, delivering ~15-20% cost reduction vs naive kv-on and moving p99 substantially lower.
2) Smallbatch is a double-edged sword: it reduces $/1k by improving GPU packing on low-to-moderate QPS, but tuning the slot duration is critical — too-long slots amplify tail latency for sporadic sessions. 150ms was near-optimal for our session shape.
3) Prefetch improves median latency at modest cost but needs a precision filter; overly-aggressive prefetch raises energy without hit-rate. We used a conservative heuristic (lambda=0.25) to keep false-prefetches <12%.
4) Hybrid stacking yields multiplicative-ish savings: kv priming reduces per-turn work, smallbatch amortizes fixed overhead, and prefetch smooths medians. Together they achieved the best $/1k in our slice but required coordination in admission control to avoid slot overcrowding.

Risk and caveats:
- Synthetic sessions: real product traffic has richer token distributions and burst correlation. Expect hit-rates to vary.
- Single-model focus: larger/smaller models will change cache amortization; results not directly transferrable.
- Interactions with multi-tenant packing and preemption weren't part of this run; production will see additional sources of jitter.

Recommendations (actionable):
- Short term (2 weeks): prototype kv-priming scheduler in canary region for one tenant class and measure real-world hit rates.
- Mid term (1 quarter): expose slot-duration and prefetch-heuristic knobs in Optimize as guarded feature flags; provide default for sessionized workloads.
- Instrumentation: add a p99-by-session-age metric and a prefetch-false-positive gauge to observability dashboards.

Runbook snippets (for reproducing):
- repo: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime (branch: needlepatch/bench)
- docker image tag: bench/2026-04-08
- loadgen cli: ./benchctl run --pattern session-poisson --qps 25 --turns 4 --tokens 12 --model open-13b-q3 --kv primed --slot 150 --prefetch 0.25

Open questions to validate with product telemetry:
- What fraction of tenants fall into the short-session, low-QPS tail that benefits most from smallbatch?
- Can we algorithmically determine priming-worthiness per tenant (expected session length > threshold)?

Appendix: raw trimmed numbers (median of trials) for QPS=25, hybrid config:
- p50: 90ms, p75: 130ms, p90: 230ms, p95: 310ms, p99: 420ms, cost: $8.7/1k

Next steps I will take:
- Wire up a 2-week canary with one internal tenant, gather real p99-by-session-age and prefetch false positive metrics. (owner: Asha)
- Draft a short utils PR to surface slot-occupancy in console per-model. (owner: Marco)
- Run same suite with Q4 quant profile and submit comparison note. (owner: Lena)

End of note.
